answer: In PoA, each identity must lock bonded collateral, making a coordinated equivocation attack economically visible. If k identities sign conflicting state, the correlated penalty grows as O(k^2), so adding agents sharply increases aggregate exposure rather than distributing it linearly. Detection then applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier across the swarm, with asymmetric depreciation driving balances toward the nadir; pulse and delta evidence link the identities and prevent cheap reconstitution.
